sentences.text: Keasius was a cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Cetorhinidae, known for its large size and filter-feeding habits.
The genus is defined by its type species, Keasius taylori, which serves as the primary reference for the group.
Welton formally described the genus Keasius in 2013.
A 2026 study identified remains of Keasius cf. septemtrionalis within a regurgitalite from the Miocene of Slovenia, pushing the known range into the southeastern central Paratethys.
This animal lived from 41.03 to 11.63 million years ago, spanning the Bartonian to Serravallian stages.
Fossil evidence shows four valid species existed across North America, Europe, and Antarctica.
